# marble.fit

> marble is a private workout journal for iPhone and iPad. Type or paste a workout in your own words, review the structured sets, and save. Free. Offline. No account, no ads.

marble turns a typed or pasted workout (gym notation, natural language, multi-day Notes, or a Hevy or Strong CSV export) into logged sets on the device, and nothing is saved until the user reviews it. It also logs sets quickly, tracks personal records, weekly goals, bodyweight, sprints, and supplements, and computes progress from the user's own training on-device.

## Key facts

- Name: marble (App Store name: marble.fit; search "marble.fit" on the App Store, because "marble" alone returns unrelated games)
- Platforms: iPhone and iPad, iOS / iPadOS 26.0 or later
- Price: Free (no subscription, no unlocks, no ads)
- Privacy: core training data stays on the device; no marble account, marble server, or third-party tracking in the app
- App Store privacy label: Data Not Collected
- Source code: public at https://github.com/enzo-prism/marble
- Offline: logging, parsing, storage, and analysis work offline
- Apple Intelligence: optional. It structures free-form prose on supported devices; gym notation and Hevy/Strong CSVs use a deterministic on-device parser on every device
- Apple Watch: there is no watch app. Apple Watch and Garmin workouts import through Apple Health
- Category: Health & Fitness
- Developer: Lorenzo Quaid Sison
- Current version and history: https://marble-fit.app/releases/

## The app

- Add: paste or type a workout (natural language, gym notation, multi-day Notes, Hevy or Strong CSV), review every workout, exercise match, set, date, RPE, rest, and note, then save. Scan a handwritten page with on-device text recognition. Resume an interrupted review.
- Log: fast set logging (weight, reps, distance, time, RPE, rest) with Log Again and Save + Next, personal-record cues while entering a set, focused workout sessions, workout history search, repeat a past workout as an editable draft, weekly split, sprint plans with tenths-precision targets and a stopwatch, calendar, supplements.
- Progress: top exercises with personal-best weights and dates, estimated 1RM trends, PR feed and rep records, weekly goal with forgiving flex-week streaks, monthly report, muscle-group coverage, bodyweight trends with per-lift DOTS, Daily Highlights end-of-day recap.
- iOS: Home Screen and Lock Screen weekly-goal widgets, Siri and Shortcuts (log a set, repeat the last set, start or finish a workout), Spotlight, Control Center / Lock Screen / Action button quick log, rest timer Live Activity with Dynamic Island controls.
- Apple Health: import Apple Watch and Garmin workouts and bodyweight; optionally export strength sessions with an effort score.
- Data: portable JSON backup and restore; progress photos and videos stay on the device.

## Frequently asked questions

- Is marble free? Yes: every feature, nothing to unlock.
- Is an account required? No.
- Does it work offline? Yes. Logging, parsing, storage, and analysis happen on the device.
- Does it need Apple Intelligence? No. Apple Intelligence improves free-form prose parsing where available; notation and CSV imports work on every device.
- Can I import from Hevy or Strong? Yes. Bring in their CSV export, review the parsed workouts, then save.
- How does it compare with Hevy or Strong? marble is free with nothing to unlock, has no account or social feed, and keeps data on the device. It has no Android or web app, no cloud sync, and no Apple Watch app.
- Does it work with Apple Watch or Garmin? Yes, through Apple Health: marble imports their workouts and can send strength sessions back with an effort score.
- Ads or tracking? The app has no ads or third-party tracking and does not sell data. Its App Store privacy label reads Data Not Collected. The website uses anonymous, aggregated Vercel Analytics.
